context: There are 3 denominations, coins = [1, 2, 5], with an unlimited supply of each. Here the target is amt = 11. The later coin change II example uses 5, and the dynamic programming table example uses 4. Find the fewest coins that make exactly 11.
description: The table on the left gives each number i and denomination coins[i-1]. The row for 1 is light orange, and the row for 5 is light green. Arrows labeled “take 1” and “take 2,” respectively, lead to a purse labeled “Target amount amt = 11.” Denomination 2 is unused. The table below translates the highlights and arrows into coin counts.
The caption reads “Optimal coin combination: 1 + 5 + 5” and “Minimum number of coins: 3.”

frames.explanation: The combination shown uses 3 coins: 1 + 5 + 5 = 11. To see why 3 is minimal, note that the largest denomination is 5. Any two coins total at most 5 + 5 = 10, short of 11. This argument follows from the input and does not appear in the original figure.
frames.title: Optimal coin combination for amount 11
